To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sea surface tilt in the Arctic Ocean and the export of buoyant Arctic waters to the North Atlantic are modulated by the annular modes of atmospheric variability.
the Arctic Ocean responds to the Northern Annular atmospheric mode by tilting the pycnocline and changing the export of fresh water to the North Atlantic.

(i) the sea-surface tilt anomaly is a response to the Ekman transport associated with an annular wind forcing, (ii) the pycnocline anomaly is a response of the sea-s surface tilt anomaly, (iii) the pycncoline anomaly can be calculated analytically from the wind forcing, and (iv) the pycncline anomaly is a good indicator of the buoyancy flux from the Arctic to the North Atlantic.

the Arctic Ocean response of sea-surface height, pycnocline, and buoyancy fluxes to the Northern Annular atmospheric mode.
the role of wind forcing in modulating the tilt and export of buoyancy in a basin of stratified, rotating fluid.
